criteria.reason: Live headless /task run: the DISPATCHED turn armed ScheduleWakeup (120s, [17]); the agent finished early and the session resumed on its notification; the final turn called ScheduleWakeup({stop:true}) ([31]) whose result reads "cancelled 1 pending wakeup(s)" ([32]), then printed COMMAND COMPLETE.

In run1 the cancellation call [31] and its result [32] come before the readout text [33] (STATE heading, then the COMMAND COMPLETE line) in the same turn; [34] result success follows and no later turn or cancellation exists.

Checked at 15:20:07, after both fallbacks were due (15:19:00 and 15:20:00): both probe session logs were last written at 15:16:58 / 15:17:54, their last assistant entry is the COMMAND COMPLETE / COMMAND STUCK banner, and no probe claude process is running. Caveat: the run2 check came only 7s after its wake time, and a headless process that has exited could not fire a wake either way; FS-1/FS-4 prove the cancellation directly.

Live headless /task run ending COMMAND STUCK: a 120s fallback was armed ([22]); the final turn called ScheduleWakeup({stop:true}) ([35]) with result "cancelled 1 pending wakeup(s)" ([36]) before the readout and the COMMAND STUCK banner. The wake-up was armed after the agent returned rather than in a DISPATCHED turn, but it was pending and was cancelled.
grep finds 13 "stop: true" matches, including .claude/rules/command-status.md:61, which sits directly after the COMPLETE/STUCK banner rules in §3; confirmed against the target tree.

Text substitution, which the criterion permits. audit-build, implement-trd, verify-build and plan each name ScheduleWakeup({ stop: true }) before the readout and banner at their final-banner exits. create-trd, audit-trd, create-prd and refine-trd contain no wake-up instruction at all (rechecked in the target tree), so nothing in them schedules past the banner or overrides command-status.md §3, which they point to for their final turn. Caveats: the exerciser did not say why live runs were impractical (only /task was run live), and its claim that notify-complete.sh carries the cancel is wrong. The cancel comes from §3, not from that script.
